scope: Read-only source review plus five focused unittest methods and one temporary-directory ownership counterexample; zero executor launches, no 1000-admission rerun, no prototype edits. Only this new review JSON is written.

blockers.location: core.py:76-79; admit checks existing owners before inserting any current-plan owners
blockers.finding: Checking only adjacent lexicographically sorted output paths does not detect every ancestor/descendant pair. An unrelated sibling with a punctuation suffix can sort between parent and child. All current-plan paths are checked only against already committed owners, so later SQL insertion does not catch the nested pair.
blockers.observed: One three-job plan admitted successfully; operational status admissions=1, ownership_claims=3; structural audit passed. No malicious SQL or tampering was required.
blockers.claim_affected: FINDINGS says exact/ancestor/descendant conflicts fail closed. Existing tests only cover nested outputs across separate admissions, not this intra-plan configuration.
blockers.recommended_fix: Validate each current-plan output against all exact parent identities in a set or equivalent component-aware structure before insertion. Add this three-output regression and a shuffled ordering variant. Structural audit may also validate static ownership invariants, while continuing to avoid historical mutable input validation.

accepted_boundaries: Canonical serialization freezes one logical caller plan and its expected digest is checked before store mutation; queue.validate_plan invokes executor.validate and rechecks declared executable and input bytes even on exact retry. Digest equality is integrity against a supplied expectation, not proof of plan approval or scientific authorization.

BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes cooperating writers. Evidence plus owner insertion commit in one transaction; five focused tests include actual process death after evidence, owners and commit. No evidence indicates split committed states under these tested boundaries. Physical power-loss/fsync interleavings remain untested as documented.

Unique attempt/output keys reject exact cross-admission duplicates. Existing ancestor parent lookups and descendant prefix range are appropriate for canonical absolute paths on this Linux cooperative filesystem boundary. The intra-plan bug is separate.

Current symlink aliases and noncanonical paths are rejected; future symlink changes, bind mounts, external attempts and post-validation input drift are explicitly outside the core. No launch authority exists.
All resume_prelaunch values other than None are rejected; exact retry still revalidates fresh outputs and fails once output exists. This intentionally conservative behavior is documented.

Mutable SQLite authoritative storage is honestly labeled trusted_index_not_historical_audit. Dropping a delete trigger and deleting owner rows changes status and structural audit catches projection mismatch. Consistent malicious rewrite/rollback is not detected and no protected head is claimed.

Structural audit checks canonical plan digest/identity and exact owner projection, not historic mutable input bytes, historic validation semantics or execution receipts. It cannot qualify a plan or authenticate an independent historical head.

nonblocking_observations.finding: The two count queries are separate SQLite reads without explicit BEGIN, so concurrent committed admission between them can yield admissions and ownership_claims from different snapshots. Treat as approximate operational counters, or wrap a read transaction if consistency is required.

SQLite Connection context managers commit/rollback but do not explicitly close; operational_status/audit/initialize rely on object lifetime for connection closure. This is a resource-management consideration, not demonstrated integrity failure.

overall: The prototype accurately limits admission-only scope and mutable-index trust, and focused tests pass. SOL-1 contradicts a central advertised ownership invariant and should be fixed before accepting the prototype as satisfying that contract. Production integration remains separately unimplemented as findings states.
